timelineEvents.title: Birth
timelineEvents.label: 5 Feb 1902 · Birth in Warsaw
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Born in Warsaw to Szmul Moszek Kaper and Maria Mucha, in a Jewish family registered in the city’s non-Christian civil records.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Born on January 23 (February 5, New Style) in Warsaw. Father – Szmul Moszek (later Stanisław/Samuel) Kaper, bookkeeper, aged 28. Mother – Maria (Mariam) née Mucha, aged 24. The family is of Jewish faith (registered at the Office of Civil Status for Non-Christian Confessions, 8th Jerusalem District, Warsaw).

timelineEvents.title: Graduation from a primary school
timelineEvents.label: 1915 · Skrynnikov school graduation
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper completes his early schooling at the private Skrynnikov school in Warsaw.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Graduates from Skrynnikov private school in Warsaw.

timelineEvents.title: High school graduation
timelineEvents.label: 1919 · Staszic Gymnasium graduation
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper graduates from Warsaw’s Staszic Gymnasium and receives his matura certificate.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Graduates from the Staszic Gymnasium in Warsaw and receives his diploma (matura certificate).

timelineEvents.title: Formal matriculation at the University of Warsaw
timelineEvents.label: 6 Feb 1920 · Formal UW matriculation
timelineEvents.shortDescription: After the one-semester delay documented separately, Kaper was formally entered in the Faculty of Law album at the University of Warsaw.
timelineEvents.longDescription: This event now records the formal matriculation rather than the earlier October 1919 application. Kaper was entered in the Faculty of Law and Political Sciences album on 6 February 1920, under album number 6854.

timelineEvents.title: Baptism
timelineEvents.label: 17 July 1920 · Baptism
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper is baptized at St. Alexander’s parish in Warsaw, marking his conversion to Catholicism.
timelineEvents.longDescription: On July 17, Kaper is baptized at the Roman Catholic Parish of St. Alexander in Warsaw, at the age of 18. The baptism marks his conversion from Judaism to Catholicism.

timelineEvents.title: War
timelineEvents.label: 1920 · Polish–Soviet War service
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper serves as a volunteer in the Polish–Soviet War before returning to university life.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Serves as a volunteer in the Polish-Soviet War in the rank of Senior Private (starszy szeregowy) in the Reserve Depot (Skadrowany Zapasowy) of the 1st Reconnaissance Aviation Regiment (1. Pułk Lotniczy Wywiadowczy), stationed at Mokotów, Warsaw. On November 5, he is granted indefinite leave as an "academic volunteer" (akademik ochotnik), allowing him to resume his university studies.

timelineEvents.title: Music studies at the Chopin Music School in Warsaw
timelineEvents.label: c. 1920–1925 · Music studies in Warsaw
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper studies piano and composition in Warsaw while building a strong theoretical musical foundation.
timelineEvents.longDescription: His training includes piano, theory, harmony, counterpoint, composition, form, and orchestration. Achieves exceptional theoretical knowledge - able to identify complex harmonies and progressions by ear alone.

timelineEvents.title: Official completion of law studies
timelineEvents.label: Feb–May 1925 · Law studies completed
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper completes his law studies, passing the final exam and receiving formal university documents.
timelineEvents.longDescription: On February 14, passes the judicial exam (egzamin prawno-sądowy) — the final of three required examinations — with a grade of "satisfactory" (dostateczny). On March 14, the Faculty of Law issues diploma no. 124. On May 26, receives his Certificate of Departure (Świadectwo Wystąpienia) no. 944.

timelineEvents.title: Public performance at the Chopin Music School concert
timelineEvents.label: 1925 · Chopin School public performance
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper performs Chopin in a public concert as a pupil of Józef Śmidowicz’s piano class.
timelineEvents.longDescription: In June, appears at a public concert of the Fryderyk Chopin Higher School of Music at the Warsaw Philharmonic as a pupil of Józef Śmidowicz’s piano class. Performs the first movement of Chopin’s Piano Concerto in F minor. Warsaw critics note his “light finger technique” and “elegance combined with concentrated lyricism,”

timelineEvents.title: First cabaret songs published
timelineEvents.label: 1926 · First cabaret songs
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper’s first Warsaw cabaret songs appear under the pseudonym Bruno Asper.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Songs for Warsaw cabarets published under the pseudonym Bruno Asper (lyrics by Andrzej Włast).

timelineEvents.title: Move to Berlin
timelineEvents.label: c. 1926 · Move to Berlin
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper leaves Warsaw for Berlin to continue his musical education and professional development.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Leaves Warsaw for Berlin to continue music education.

timelineEvents.title: Performance of piano pieces
timelineEvents.label: 1928 · Piano pieces performed in Warsaw
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Eliza Rozenblum performs three unidentified piano pieces by Kaper at the Warsaw Conservatory Hall.
timelineEvents.longDescription: At the Warsaw Conservatory Hall, Eliza Rozenblum performs three piano pieces by Kaper (titles unknown).

timelineEvents.title: University admission delayed by a disciplinary sanction
timelineEvents.label: Delayed UW matriculation
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper’s admission to the Faculty of Law at the University of Warsaw was delayed by a one-semester disciplinary sanction before his formal matriculation in February 1920.
timelineEvents.longDescription: University records show that Kaper applied to the Faculty of Law at the University of Warsaw in October 1919, but that the Matriculation Commission rejected his immediate admission after a disciplinary incident. The sanction was temporary: he later described it in his curriculum vitae as a one-semester relegation, and he was formally entered in the faculty album on 6 February 1920.

timelineEvents.title: Police certificate records Mosaic religion
timelineEvents.label: Mosaic religion recorded
timelineEvents.shortDescription: A police certificate issued shortly before Kaper’s baptism recorded his religion as “Mosaic,” the official term then used for the Jewish faith.
timelineEvents.longDescription: The certificate of good conduct issued by the Warsaw State Police forms an important documentary link between Kaper’s university records and the later baptismal entry. It anchors the discussion of identity in administrative sources rather than retrospectively imposed narratives: Kaper appears in the record as a young Warsaw student from an assimilated Jewish family whose formal confessional status changed only a few months later.
